afo-carbon-eval.title: AFO/Carbon Evaluation
afo-carbon-eval.text:
Patient presents at North/South office for evaluation of progressive gait instability, lower extremity weakness, and frequent tripping/falls impacting daily activities. He/She has been diagnosed with foot drop Left/Right due to {Diagnosis: Spinal stenosis/Muscular Dystrophy/Peripheral Neuropathy/Post-Stroke Hemiplegia/Multiple Sclerosis/Charcot-Marie-Tooth/CP}. Patient experiences persistent foot drop during the swing phase of gait and muscle fatigue after walking short distances. Current off-the-shelf bracing or lack of bracing provides inadequate energy return and insufficient stability to control dynamic gait deviations. Ambulation is limited to {Ambulation Distance: <100 feet/100-300 feet/300+ feet/community distances} {Assistance: unassisted/with a cane/with a walker} before requiring rest due to fatigue.

Pt. was examined and Left/Right lower extremity assessment revealed dorsiflexion MMT strength of {MMT Dorsiflexion: 0/1/2/2+/3/3+/4/5}. Plantarflexion MMT strength was {MMT Plantarflexion: 0/1/2/2+/3/3+/4/5/WNL}. Knee extensor strength was {MMT Knee Extensors: 3/3+/4/4+/5}. Passive range of motion to neutral (0° dorsiflexion) is {ROM Neutral: achievable with knee extended/achievable with knee flexed/limited}. Severe fixed equinus deformity is {Fixed Deformity: absent/present} and dynamic fluctuating edema is {Edema: absent/present}. Skin integrity is {Skin Integrity: intact/intact with mild erythema/compromised}.

Gait evaluation reveals {Gait Pattern: steppage gait/slap foot at initial contact/knee hyperextension during stance phase/lack of heel-strike} affecting the Left/Right lower extremity during swing and stance phases.

Due to lower extremity weakness and foot drop with high fall risk, patient requires a dynamic carbon fiber AFO (L1951). Standard polypropylene AFOs are inadequate due to the patient's need for dynamic energy storage and return during stance-to-swing transition to reduce fatigue and stabilize gait. Patient meets all Medicare LCD coverage criteria, including ambulatory status, absence of severe fixed deformity or severe edema, and adequate knee/hip strength to manage dynamic propulsion.

Plan: Fit and adjust HCPCS L1951 (carbon fiber dynamic response AFO) to affected Left/Right lower extremity(ies). Custom modifications to include footplate trimming, heel height alignment, and shoe interface fitting. Patient instructed on donning/doffing, skin monitoring, and footwear requirements. Follow-up scheduled in {Follow-up: 2 weeks/4 weeks}.

diabetic-shoe-eval.title: Diabetic Shoe Evaluation
diabetic-shoe-eval.text:
Patient presents at North/South office for therapeutic diabetic footwear and insert evaluation. He/She has a documented history of Diabetes Mellitus with secondary qualifying conditions. Patient is ambulatory and requires protective footwear to prevent foot ulceration, skin breakdown, and lower extremity complications.

Physical examination of the feet reveals the presence of {Qualifying Condition: peripheral neuropathy with evidence of callus/history of pre-ulcerative callus/history of previous foot ulceration/foot deformity/poor circulation/history of partial foot amputation}.

Foot Examination & Biomechanical Assessment:

Skin & Tissue Integrity: Skin is {Skin Integrity: intact/intact with localized hyperkeratotic callus/noted with healed ulcer site}. No active open ulcerations present.

Deformities: 
Assessment reveals {Deformity: no rigid deformities/bunions (hallux valgus)/hammer toes/Charcot foot/pes planus/metatarsal head prominence}.

Vascular/Sensation: Monofilament testing demonstrates {Sensation: loss of protective sensation/intact sensation}. Distal pulses are {Pulses: palpable/diminished}.

Foot Structure & Sizing: 
Brannock device and anatomical measurements taken in weight-bearing position. Footwear size determined: Left/Right/Bilateral size {Shoe Size: 6/6.5/7/7.5/8/8.5/9/9.5/10/10.5/11/11.5/12/12.5/13/13.5/14} and width {Shoe Width: Medium (D)/Wide (2E)/Extra Wide (4E)/6E}.

Medical Necessity:
Patient has Diabetes Mellitus with a documented qualifying lower extremity condition certified by the physician managing their diabetic care.

Patient requires therapeutic depth shoes (A5500 x 2) to accommodate structural foot topography, prevent friction/shear, and reduce peak plantar pressures.

Patient requires {Insert Selection: A5512 (prefabricated, heat molded) / A5513 (custom-molded tri-laminate)} inserts (x 6 inserts / 3 pairs) to provide total contact pressure redistribution, arch support, and shock absorption across the plantar surface.

Plan:
Order HCPCS A5500 x 2 (Therapeutic diabetic depth shoes) and HCPCS {Insert Selection: A5512/A5513} x 6 (Therapeutic inserts). ______

Custom fit and mold inserts to patient's feet/shoes using weight-bearing trial. Accommodations and adjustments performed to ensure complete plantar contact without focal pressure points.

Patient instructed on break-in schedule (1–2 hours daily with gradual increase), daily visual foot inspections using a mirror, proper socks, and donning/doffing procedures.

Follow-up scheduled in {Follow-up: 2 weeks/4 weeks} or immediately if erythema or skin irritation occurs.

tlso-cash.title: TLSO-Cash/Jewett

custom-1786401952325.title: CROW boot delivery
custom-1786401952325.text: Patient was seen at the North/South office for fitting and delivery of Charcot/Crow boot.   He/she was fit with a custom CROW orthosis. The device is reasonable and necessary to stabilize the hindfoot, midfoot, and ankle joints in the sagittal and coronal planes, decrease severe subtalar joint motion/pain, prevent joint collapse during ambulation, and help to slow progression or Charcot arthropathy. He/she was provided with verbal and written use and care instructions, taught proper donning/doffing, and instructed on a progressive wearing schedule while monitoring skin for irritation.

clavicle-strap.text: Patient was seen at the North/South office for fitting and delivery of a Left/Right figure-8 clavicle strap/support orthosis from {Brand / Manufacturer: Breg / DonJoy / Ossur / DJO} for clavicle fracture / acromioclavicular injury. Device is reasonable and necessary to immobilize the shoulder girdle, maintain reduction, and promote bony healing. Instructed on skin monitoring and strap adjustment.
clavicle-strap.title: Clavicle Support

forearm-splint.text: Patient was seen at the North/South office for fitting and delivery of an extended Left/Right forearm and wrist orthosis from {Brand / Manufacturer: Breg / DonJoy / Ossur / DJO / Hely & Weber} for distal radius / forearm fracture / severe tendonitis. He/she was fit with a {Size: Ped./XXS/XSmall/Small/Med/Large/XL/2XL/3XL/4XL} forearm splint. Rigid palmar and dorsal stays contoured to patient's anatomy. Device is reasonable and necessary to immobilize the wrist and distal forearm in functional alignment, minimize painful musculoskeletal strain, and protect healing osseous structures during ADLs. Instructed on wear schedule and skin care.

humeral-fracture-brace.text: Patient was seen at the North/South office for fitting and delivery of a Left/Right prefabricated rigid humeral fracture brace (Sarmiento) from {Brand / Manufacturer: Breg / DonJoy / Ossur / DJO / Corflex} for diaphyseal humerus fracture management. He/she was fit with a {Size: Ped./XXS/XSmall/Small/Med/Large/XL/2XL/3XL/4XL} humeral orthosis with shoulder suspension cap and circumferential compression straps. Circumferential soft tissue compression and rigid anterior/posterior shells provide hydrodynamic support to stabilize the humeral shaft fracture, maintain anatomical alignment, and permit active shoulder/elbow motion. He/she was instructed on strap tensioning, skin inspection, and progressive wearing schedule. Follow-up PRN.

knee-immobilizer.text: Patient was seen at the North/South office for fitting and delivery of a Left/Right tri-panel rigid knee immobilizer from {Brand / Manufacturer: Breg / DonJoy / Ossur / DJO / Medline} for acute knee injury / post-surgical stabilization. He/she was fit with a {Size: Ped./XXS/XSmall/Small/Med/Large/XL/2XL/3XL/4XL} knee immobilizer ({Length: 12 inch / 16 inch / 20 inch / 22 inch / 24 inch}). Posterior and medial/lateral contoured aluminum stays adjusted to hold knee in full extension. Device is reasonable and necessary to immobilize the knee in the sagittal plane, protect healing ligamentous/tendinous repairs, and prevent weightbearing collapse during early recovery. Instructed on proper donning/doffing and skin checks.
knee-immobilizer.title: Knee Immobilizer

tibial-fracture-brace.text: Patient was seen at the North/South office for fitting and delivery of a Left/Right rigid tibial fracture orthosis (Sarmiento AFO) from {Brand / Manufacturer: Breg / DonJoy / Ossur / DJO / Townsend} for closed tibial shaft fracture management. He/she was fit with a {Size: Ped./XXS/XSmall/Small/Med/Large/XL/2XL/3XL/4XL} tibial fracture brace with anterior/posterior shells and footplate. The rigid circumferential shells provide hydrostatic tissue compression, control sagittal/coronal angular alignment, and offload the fracture site to promote bone union while allowing protected ambulation. Instructed on skin inspection, donning/doffing, and wearing protocol. Follow-up PRN.
tibial-fracture-brace.title: Tibial Fracture Orthosis
